https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Cigarettes in Australian-style plain packaging are being counterfeited at factories in Cambodia, according to intelligence provided to the federal government. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA View image in fullscreen Cigarettes in Australian-style plain packaging are being counterfeited at factories in Cambodia, according to intelligence provided to the federal government. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Australia news Illegal tobacco increasingly hard to spot, with some fakes in plain packaging featuring Australian health warnings Government warned that counterfeit tobacco produced by criminal organisations in south-east Asia is becoming more sophisticated Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian Associated Press Wed 14 Oct 2026 19.32 EDT Last modified on Wed 14 Oct 2026 20.54 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The black-market tobacco trade continues to thrive as sellers turn to counterfeit packaging to skirt bans, prompting calls for the urgent passing of tougher laws. Intelligence provided to the federal government shows cigarettes in plain Australian-style packaging are being produced illegally at an industrial scale in south-east Asian warehouses. Experts weigh in on how to tackle illicit tobacco – and why an 80% excise cut is not on their list Read more Factories owned and operated by criminal syndicates, primarily based in Cambodia, are pumping out increasingly sophisticated fake products that replicate common brands. Some of the counterfeit packaging is even branded with Australian health warnings. View image in fullscreen Julian Hill has urged parliament to pass laws giving authorities new powers to target the illicit tobacco trade. Photograph: ABF Media The production has prompted the customs minister, Julian Hill, to urge parliament to pass tough laws as soon as possible. A new bill on the tobacco trade is expected to be debated in the Senate on Thursday. It would give law enforcement stronger powers to detect and disrupt illegal tobacco trade lines, including choking off criminal profits. But Hill was concerned the sophisticated overseas production of cigarettes was becoming increasingly hard to detect or stop. “Serious and organised criminal syndicates have weaponised the cheap oversupply of tobacco globally and will do anything to make a buck,” he said. “The crooks will continue to adapt their tactics. “This highlights the urgency of equipping state, territory and commonwealth authorities with these new powers to go after anyone involved in the illegal tobacco trade, including the supply chains and retail outlets,” he said. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion Several states and territories have been cracking down on enforcement measures, including blitzes of black-market shopfronts. Queensland has taken the hardest line and legal cigarette sales have grown as a result. NSW police closed 10 retailers across the state last week, including eight in south-west Sydney. Across just two days on 6 and 7 October, NSW health inspectors seized 420,000 illegal cigarettes, about 60kg of loose-leaf tobacco and thousands of illicit vapes – small numbers compared with the 2.4 tonnes of tobacco confiscated since the start of the year. Some shops have been closed for more than 90 days as the NSW government ramps up enforcement. http://www.jpost.com/international/artic.text: Polish police have detained a man suspected of planning an attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk, the Interior Minister said on Sunday, after it warned earlier of a threat to Tusk and Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz."The man who threatened and planned an attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk has been detained by Polish police," Marcin Kierwinski wrote on X, without giving further details.Tusk thanked the police for "swift and decisive action" in a separate post on X.Mężczyzna grożący zamachem został zatrzymany. Dziękuję policjantom za szybkie i zdecydowane działanie.— Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) October 11, 2026While violent crime is relatively rare in Poland, the country is deeply polarized politically and has faced security threats due to its proximity to the war in Ukraine.In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of calling for the assassination of senior Polish politicians.Tusk reported threats following assassination attempt on Slovak PM in 2024In 2024, Tusk said he received threats after an assassination attempt on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico.Interior Ministry Spokesperson Karolina Galecka said on Sunday an email with information about the potential attack had been forwarded to police by the State Protection Service, which is responsible for ministers' security.

Mexico: spectacular Catrina parade brings the dead to life Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 26/10/2026 - 11:03 GMT+1 Skeleton faces, extravagant headdresses and dazzling costumes transformed Mexico City's streets into a colourful spectacle. The annual Catrinas Parade celebrates the country's Day of the Dead traditions. … More Wearing extravagant headdresses , glittering gowns and painted skull faces transformed Mexico City's Paseo de la Reforma into a colourful procession on Sunday, 25 October, as thousands took part in the annual Catrinas Parade . ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Dancers , couples dressed as skeletal brides and grooms , and even costumed dogs made their way through cheering crowds. Some participants wore illuminated outfits , while others displayed elaborate embroidery and striking headpieces . Make-up artists worked behind the scenes to create the distinctive Catrina look , with full face designs taking between 20 and 40 minutes. The parade celebrates La Catrina , a skeletal figure created by illustrator José Guadalupe Posada more than a century ago and later popularised by artist Diego Rivera . Once a satire of European-inspired fashion, she has become one of Mexico's best-known cultural symbols . The event forms part of the build-up to Día de los Muertos , celebrated mainly on 1 and 2 November, when families honour deceased relatives with altars, flowers, candles and offerings . Mexico City is preparing an even larger parade on 31 October , with more than 4,000 performers , 12 floats and two giant balloons expected. The capital's Zócalo will also feature a 32-metre Catrina surrounded by millions of marigolds . The festivities combine music, creativity and remembrance , turning the commemoration of the dead into a celebration of life . https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/12/russ.text: On Thursday, a Russian serviceman was killed in a car explosion in St Petersburg, Russia. The local office of the Investigative Committee said the cause had not yet been established and announced that it had opened a murder investigation.The blast comes as Moscow accuses Kyiv of carrying out a series of killings of Russian military personnel since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.The Ukrainian armed forces have claimed responsibility for some of the killings, while remaining silent about others.The attacks have involved booby-trapped cars, explosives hidden in scooters and shootings.The serviceman, whose rank has not been officially disclosed, died as a result of “a car explosion in the Pushkinsky district” of St Petersburg, the Investigative Committee said in a press release.“A murder investigation into the serviceman’s death has been launched,” the committee added.“At present, investigators and forensic experts, together with operational officers, are examining the scene and a number of necessary forensic tests are being ordered. All the circumstances of what happened are being clarified,” it said on Telegram.Russian media reported that the explosion took place in the settlement of Shushary on Kolpinskoye Highway. They said the man killed was a colonel in the Russian armed forces and chief navigator of the 6th Air and Air Defence Army.According to Russian media, the serviceman was alone and driving the car when it exploded. The explosive device had been attached to the underside of the car and was detonated remotely as he was leaving a courtyard. He died at the scene. The moment of the blast was captured by an intercom camera.On 27 August 2026, in the Slavyanka district of the same settlement, a lieutenant colonel, also from the air and air defence forces, was blown up together with his wife. Both lost their legs. The lieutenant colonel died at the scene, while his wife was saved by doctors.At the time, a 24-year-old Russian woman who had left for Turkey after the explosion was suspected of planting the bomb. Law enforcement agencies did not officially comment on the progress of the investigation and did not release the victim’s name or other details.The man killed in August was reportedly (source in Russian) 43-year-old Sergei Sechkov, who served in the 332nd Separate Guards Helicopter Regiment. His father confirmed to the independent Russian outlet Agentstvo that his son had died in the blast.In May 2022, the Main Intelligence Directorate of Ukraine’s Defence Ministry accused (source in Russian) servicemen from the regiment of carrying out missile and bomb strikes on Ukrainian civilians on the Slobozhansky axis.Series of targeted attacks on Russian military personnelThe highest-ranking Russian officer to have been targeted since the start of the full-scale war was Lieutenant General Igor Kirillov, who was killed near his flat in Moscow in December 2024.On that occasion, Ukraine explicitly claimed responsibility for killing Kirillov, whom Kyiv accused of ordering the use of chemical weapons against Ukrainian troops. Russian President Vladimir Putin called the incident “a serious failure” on the part of Russia’s security services.In April 2025, Lieutenant General Yaroslav Moskalyk was killed when his car exploded in Balashikha, near Moscow.In December that year, Lieutenant General Fanil Sarvarov was blown up outside his home, just 16km from the Kremlin.In February 2026, Lieutenant General Vladimir Alexeyev, first deputy head of the Main Directorate of the Russian General Staff, was shot at in the lobby of a Moscow apartment building as he was leaving his flat.In April, a battalion commander from a training communications unit was killed when a device planted in a post box exploded on the grounds of a military garrison in Russia’s Khabarovsk region.On 1 August 2026, Aleksandr Chaiko, who had been appointed head of Russia’s Aerospace Forces in May, was named as the intended target of a high-profile assassination attempt. The blast took place at the Balzi Rossi restaurant in one of Stalin’s “Seven Sisters” skyscrapers, on Barrikadnaya Street.
